messages:
maria_cse: FYI OrbitPay just escalated — their webhooks to our API started returning 403s around 02:15 UTC after last night's maintenance. They say their allowlist no longer matches our egress IPs. 

maria_cse: customer provided one failed curl example:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/webhook -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"evt":"charge.succeeded"}'
# they see a 403 from their firewall side (no request in their logs)
```

jen_oncall: copying in net infra. @raj_netinfra can you confirm if any NAT/egress rotation happened in the 01:30-02:30 UTC window? :mag_right: 

raj_netinfra: I see a NAT pool reallocation during autoscale at 02:12 UTC in us-west-2. There was a cleanup job that reclaimed unused elastic IPs and reattached a different set to the NAT gateway.

raj_netinfra: current egress set for the VPC that serves OrbitPay: 34.198.12.9, 34.198.12.10, 34.198.12.11 (previously 35.199.23.45/46/47).

maria_cse: customer only had the old three IPs on their allowlist. They haven't seen our new IPs show up on their side, so their firewall is dropping traffic (403). They asked for an emergency unblock.

jen_oncall: pinged OrbitPay to ask them to temporarily add the new three IPs and to share a tcpdump if they still don't see traffic. Waiting on reply. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

tim_reliability: root cause looks like the unattended terraform cleanup job that pruned unused EIPs ran during the scale event and caused EIP reassignment. We should treat reserved EIPs for customers with allowlists as sticky.

raj_netinfra: immediate remediation options:
- ask customer to add new IPs (fastest)
- reassign previous EIPs back (requires reattaching and may disrupt other tenants)
- promote OrbitPay to reserved NAT allocation (longer-term, creates static egress)

maria_cse: OrbitPay asked for the quick add. They confirmed they can update their allowlist if we provide the list and a verification method.

raj_netinfra: provided verification steps to customer: from within their network, confirm they see requests from our new IPs by checking firewall logs for outbound connections to api.redwood.ai timestamps 02:10-02:30 UTC. Also we can POST to a temporary echo endpoint and have them share the source IP.

maria_cse: sent the IPs + verification instructions. Customer updated and reports success. Webhooks are now flowing. They saw requests arriving from 34.198.12.9 at 02:20 UTC. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: detected terraform job "infra/cleanup-eips" completed at 02:11 UTC (run-id: tf-20260211-2211).

tim_reliability: action items:
- (P0->P1) add guardrails to prevent the cleanup job from touching EIPs attached to NATs in production serving customers with allowlists.
- create a support flow to offer reserved NAT IPs for customers on strict allowlists.
- add a churn alert when >30% of egress IPs change within 1 hour for a VPC.

raj_netinfra: I'll open infra ticket with proposed terraform policy change and a playbook for emergency reattaches.

maria_cse: closing the incident with OrbitPay — they confirmed success and requested the reserved NAT option for future. I'll follow up on billing + provisioning steps.

jen_oncall: thanks team. Logging post-incident notes and handshake with product for reserved NAT offering. :memo: 

maria_cse: TL;DR: NAT EIP rotation during cleanup caused egress IP drift -> customer allowlist blocked webhooks -> temporary fix: customer added new IPs -> long-term fix: reserved NAT / terraform guardrails.
